model: Zyot Decider v3 4B (Gemma 3 4B + LoRA) — local GGUF Q4_K_M + LoRA GGUF f16
prompt_style: copy-task (pick FIRST letter from preferred list; boolean-decision-shaped)

latency.notes: 5.5x faster than planning-prompt version (was 2203ms). Smaller prompt (237 vs 470 chars) = less prefill.

verdict.correction_from_previous_report: Previous report said Zyot v3 'can't chase food because it's a decision classifier, not spatial planner'. That was WRONG framing — Jev and Kev are also decision classifiers, not spatial planners.
verdict.actual_root_cause: The prior 'planning' prompt asked the model to REASON about spatial state. The model tolerated but didn't follow the preferred-direction hint. This prompt asks it to COPY the first letter of a shortlist — the same shape as its training data (boolean/typed decisions).
verdict.story: Zyot v3 4B is a competent snake agent when the task is framed as a shortlist selection instead of spatial planning. 13 food eaten, length 16, 100% legal moves, 355ms/decision.
